title: Checkout database connection pool exhaustion
snippet: When checkout requests fail with database connection pool exhaustion, verify active database connections and pool utilization. Check for connection leaks or long-running transactions. Increase pool capacity only after confirming database capacity. Restart affected application instances if connections remain stuck.
recommended_checks: Check active and idle database connections
recommended_actions: Increase connection pool capacity if database capacity permits
Restart affected application instances if required
rollback_notes: If increasing the pool causes database saturation, revert the pool configuration and restore the previous capacity.

title: Order service Redis dependency failure
snippet: When order creation reports Redis connection failures, verify Redis availability, connectivity, and connection limits. Check whether the service can reach the Redis endpoint. Use application fallback behavior only if the fallback is known to be safe.
recommended_actions: Use cache fallback only when supported
rollback_notes: Do not disable cache validation or bypass Redis permanently without confirming application consistency requirements.

title: External payment gateway degradation
snippet: For payment gateway timeouts or HTTP 503 responses, verify external gateway health and request latency. Check whether failures are isolated to the gateway. Validate retry and fallback behavior before changing application configuration.
recommended_checks: Compare gateway latency with normal baseline
recommended_actions: Contact or monitor the external gateway provider
rollback_notes: Avoid increasing retry counts aggressively because retries can amplify load during external dependency degradation.

title: User service database latency
snippet: When user profile requests become slow without a significant application error increase, investigate database query latency, active connections, and resource utilization. Identify slow queries before making database configuration changes.
rollback_notes: Database configuration changes should be reversible and validated against query performance before wider rollout.

title: Inventory downstream dependency degradation
snippet: When inventory requests fail because of a downstream dependency, verify the dependency health and connectivity before changing the inventory application. Use retry or fallback mechanisms only when explicitly supported.
recommended_actions: Use a safe fallback if available
rollback_notes: Do not bypass dependency validation if doing so can result in incorrect inventory information.

title: Notification message queue backlog
snippet: For delayed notifications, check queue depth, consumer throughput, and consumer health. If the queue is growing and consumers are healthy but under-capacity, scale consumers gradually and monitor backlog recovery.
rollback_notes: Scale down consumers gradually after backlog returns to normal to avoid unnecessary resource usage.

title: Search cluster degradation
snippet: When search requests fail or become slow, inspect cluster health, shard availability, node resource pressure, and cluster errors. Identify unhealthy nodes before restarting or replacing infrastructure.
recommended_actions: Scale the search cluster if sustained resource pressure is confirmed
rollback_notes: Cluster changes should be reversible. Avoid removing healthy nodes during an active incident.

title: Identity and token dependency failure
snippet: For authentication failures caused by identity or token dependencies, verify identity provider availability, token service health, and network connectivity. Do not disable authentication validation as a workaround.
rollback_notes: Never bypass authentication validation or weaken security controls as an incident workaround.

title: Recommendation service resource saturation
snippet: When recommendation latency increases alongside sustained CPU and memory utilization, identify resource-intensive workloads. Scale instances when appropriate and investigate whether a workload or model operation is consuming excessive resources.
recommended_actions: Monitor CPU and memory after scaling
rollback_notes: Scale changes should be reversible. Do not terminate instances until sufficient healthy capacity is available.

title: Checkout deployment regression
snippet: If checkout errors increase immediately after a deployment while dependencies remain healthy, compare the current release with the previous known-good version. Validate configuration changes and consider rollback when a regression is confirmed.
recommended_checks: Check deployment timestamp against error increase
recommended_actions: Roll back the release when regression is confirmed
rollback_notes: The preferred rollback target is the previous known-good release and configuration.

title: Insufficient evidence investigation
snippet: When an incident description and available evidence do not identify a clear failure domain, do not guess the root cause. Request additional context such as representative request IDs, exact error messages, affected endpoints, timestamps, and dependency information.
recommended_actions: Continue diagnosis after sufficient evidence is available
rollback_notes: No remediation should be executed when the failure domain cannot be established with sufficient confidence.

title: Conflicting payment incident evidence
snippet: When payment incidents contain evidence of both external dependency degradation and internal resource pressure, do not select a single root cause without additional evidence. Separate observed symptoms from hypotheses and request targeted investigation.
recommended_checks: Compare gateway latency with application resource utilization
Check whether gateway failures correlate with CPU pressure
recommended_actions: Proceed only after the dominant failure mechanism is established
rollback_notes: Do not execute remediation based solely on conflicting evidence.
